items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1960
items.q: My first trumpet player died. And the other one I had, Mud Carey, came to New Orleans

ctx.x: Mr. Deer, we'd like for you to tell us, for instance, when these white musicians picked up jazz from the Cullen Boys.

Well, they used to come to those places nightly, and they got them so good so they'd say, Well, Deer, you want to take a walk around the block? I said, Yes. Go ahead. I'll rest you up. I'll play clarinet. And so the rest of the instruments, the other boys would rest them up like that. That's the way they started. Mr. Deer, when you were in the Warriors, did you happen to meet Buddy Bolger? I'm sure he must have run into him. Oh, yes. And New Orleans knows about him. items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: I knew Mutt very well. Wonderful trumpet playing.

ctx.x: Mutt Cherry died up there, too. Yes, he died in 1948, I think, September of 1948. Sam was pretty good there.
I knew Mutt very well. Wonderful trumpet playing. His style of playing.
Mutt. I wanted to ask you a few questions about your life. I was from Hornville.
